note: RimPLC ladder (v2). "i think this is the whoole PLC like logic chain if this then this if heath level reaches then this type of thing for the whole game properly layed out into a PLC that we will call RimPLC" -- laid out as a PLC: `sensors` are the measured inputs (gates.py derive(); a key it cannot read is left out and the rung stays quiet), `tags` are constants (owner-only safety limits) and variables (setpoints recomputed each scan, clamped, overridable with ladder_set tag), `marks` are what she records herself with ladder_set mark (booleans or numbers), and `gates` are the rungs: when (an AND over sensors, marks and tags; ops = exact, <, >, <=, >=, !=) -> then (an ordered action chain). Lower priority fires first; only the first live rung plus `always` is handed over. A rung with latch:true gets mark_<id>_done:false in its when and sets it as its last step, so a finished growth rung never hides the rungs after it. Rungs at GRACE_FROM_PRIORITY and above (except always) wait until day > START_GRACE_DAYS. Anything marked UNVERIFIED in a note has not been seen in a captured bridge reply or the mod's wiki. Control chains (owner decision 3, docs/RIMPLC_DESIGN.md): rungs with a `chain` field (combat, medical, repairs, defense, supply) are wired like relays -- each rung's last steps set a mark that is the next rung's input, a reset rung drops the latch when the condition clears; every chain rung is `mode: advise` and carries `check` (the question it answers) and `notice` (a one-line message for a human).

tags.note: PLC tag table. CONSTANTS are safety limits: owner only, ladder_set refuses them. VARIABLES are setpoints: gates.py recomputes the ones with a size rule from measured state each scan, clamps every value to min/max, and her ladder_set tag override wins inside those bounds. Reference them in a rung's when as {NAME}, or use a tag name directly as a when key.

MEAL_BILL_TARGET.rule: owner: "cook bill maintained at 50 rather than 10"

BEDS_NEEDED.rule: one per colonist, plus one spare

COOLERS_PER_ROOM.rule: one per room up to 3 rooms, then one per 2 rooms

FIELD_CELLS_PER_PAWN.rule: fixed setpoint; rice yield per cell UNVERIFIED, so 40 is a margin

CORPSE_LIMIT.rule: fixed setpoint (mood penalty for seen corpses)

TARGET_TITLE.rule: fixed setpoint: 6 = Baron (rank list after Count UNVERIFIED)

CAVALRY_ENABLED.rule: 1 on, 0 off (cavalry-check sets 0 when no mount gizmo exists)

POD_SQUAD.rule: fixed setpoint: one pawn per pod

POD_FUEL.rule: 150 x POD_SQUAD (cost per tile UNVERIFIED, generous)

GRAV_PARTS_TARGET.rule: placeholder: set after counting what the console requires (UNVERIFIED)

FIGHT_RATIO_MIN.rule: fixed setpoint: able shooters per hostile to take the fight

CALL_HELP_RATIO.rule: fixed setpoint: under this many shooters per hostile it is 'too many' -- call help or retreat

marks.note: What the bridge cannot measure without moving the selection or opening a UI. She reads it on purpose during a turn and records it with ladder_set mark. A boolean mark never set reads false; a numeric mark reads its default below.

numeric.start_kind: 1 Crashlanded, 2 Lost Tribe, 3 Naked Brutality, 4 Async Industries, 5 The Store, 6 Lone survivor (read off the new-colony screen)
numeric.title_rank: 0 none, 1 Freeholder, 2 Yeoman, 3 Acolyte, 4 Knight, 5 Praetor, 6 Baron, 7 Count ... (after Count UNVERIFIED)
numeric.mounts_trained: animals with Obedience + Release done (Animals tab)
numeric.store_approach: 1 seal the basement, 2 supervised search, 3 document and ask for help
numeric.combat_plan: combat chain latch: 0 not chosen, 1 fight, 2 hold for help, 3 kite, 4 help called, 5 retreat
